text: Lesson 3 covered writing custom producer and consumer code. But most integrations aren't custom — thousands of teams solve the same problem identically. Kafka Connect exists so none of them write that by hand.

Every connector runs in one of two directions. A source connector watches an external system and turns changes into Kafka messages. A sink connector reads from a topic and writes into an external system.

Connect runs as a cluster of workers, and each connector is a JSON description of what to run. connector.class picks the implementation; tasks.max controls parallelism. Retries and offsets are handled for you.
Before writing a config, you'd browse what already exists — Confluent Cloud's connector catalog, showing search results for pre-built connectors ready to configure.
Instead of asking how to write a producer, the question becomes whether a connector already exists — and for most common systems, it does. Next up: a real source and sink connector pair.
